LLM_description:
Situation:
Combined Task Force East is conducting mobile defense across a contested sector. Forward units along the Riverline corridor and the Hill 402 ridgeline require immediate resupply of ammunition and fuel to sustain maneuver and fires. Multiple rear-area depots (e.g., Supply Depot Bravo near the railhead, Depot Charlie at the logistics node, Depot Echo at the highway junction) can dispatch convoys. The road network includes choke points exposed to indirect fire and urban segments with IED risk. Weather and ongoing route clearance operations constrain movement windows. Some depots have throughput limits, and several units have elevated consumption following recent contact.

Mission:
Resupply designated front-line units (e.g., 3rd Infantry Battalion, 5th Armored Cavalry Squadron, 11th Field Artillery Battery) from available depots during the current resupply cycle while minimizing total operational cost (transport + shortage penalties + vehicle deployment + fixed route security risk costs).

Execution/Concept:
- We will allocate flows of each supply class from depots to units over available ground routes. Depot dispatches are constrained by stock and throughput; unit demands must be covered, with controlled shortfalls permitted when operationally acceptable.
- Vehicles can only move on routes formally activated for the period. Activating any route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost for security overhead—escort teams, EOD/route clearance, ISR overwatch—regardless of the number of vehicles that traverse that route. We will consolidate loads to minimize the number of activated routes, balancing risk exposure against demand urgency.
- Vehicle capacity limits and supply volumes drive packing decisions; heavier/bulkier items reduce per-vehicle throughput. Vehicle deployment incurs a cost distinct from route transport costs.
- Transport costs vary by depot-to-unit route based on distance, terrain, and congestion. Where risk costs are prohibitive, we may accept limited shortfalls if the penalty is lower than the combined transport, vehicle, and route activation costs.
- Fleet size is limited; total vehicles assigned across all routes cannot exceed available fleet. Movement Control will sequence convoys, deconflict corridors, and adjust routing if interdiction or closures occur.
- Priorities: sustain ammunition for maneuver and fire support units; maintain fuel for armored mobility; avoid high-risk corridors unless required for mission-critical units. Depots with lower route risk or cost will be used first; high-risk routes will only be activated when benefits outweigh fixed risk overhead.
- Coordination: Depot Operations prepare loads by supply type; Movement Control activates routes and tasks vehicles; Route Clearance and Escort elements are aligned to each activated corridor; unit S4s stage reception and onward distribution.
